item.title: A global 0.1-degree gridded dataset of single and compound temperature and precipitation extremes from 1950 to 2025
item.description:
Shilei Peng, Songping Luo, Bin Wang, Zhixiong Tang, Qingqing Dai, Kunihito Mihara, Jing Du, Shenghui Geng, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08312-x
Abstract Extreme weather and climate events are increasingly intensified by human-induced global warming, exacerbating risks to ecosystems and society. Yet many global extremes datasets remain coarse and fragmented, limiting local assessments of temperature and precipitation hazards. Here we introduce ERA5-EX, a global 0.1° gridded dataset of single and compound temperature and precipitation extremes from 1950 to 2025 derived from ERA5-Land. ERA5-EX provides 34 annual variables comprising 26 indices from Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices, and eight bivariate metrics that quantify occurrence days for compound wet-hot, wet-cold, dry-hot, dry-cold, warm day-night, cold day-night, warm-heavy rain, and cold-heavy rain events. We also release the ERA5-EX tool, a Python workflow for tiled global or regional processing from daily inputs through index and compound event generation, feature extraction, and map and time series visualization. Technical evaluation is provided through intercomparison with observationally constrained gridded extremes products for single indices and with publicly available compound event datasets where definitions overlap. The ERA5-EX dataset and tool serve to support climate monitoring and risk assessment.

item.title: The Encanto Neighborhood Field Experiments Dataset: Land–Atmosphere Interactions in Urban Phoenix
item.description:
Katia Lamer, Edwin V. Davis, Zackary Mages, Nidia E. Rojas-Robles, Enrique R. Vivoni, Maria Cadeddu, Zhaocheng Wang, Khayrun N. Mitu, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08464-w
Abstract Urban environments exhibit strong spatial heterogeneity in surface properties and morphology, driving complex land–atmosphere interactions at neighborhood scales that remain poorly documented. The Encanto Neighborhood field experiments were designed to address this gap by collecting spatially dense, multi-dimensional and multi-parameteric observations across a ~3 × 3 km domain in Phoenix, Arizona. The dataset combines fixed, mobile, and balloon-borne measurements of atmospheric properties near the surface and at various heights in the column, as well as measurements of turbulent exchanges and land surface properties. This work also contributes a technique that transforms irregular mobile temperature measurements into continuous, high-resolution temperature fields, enabling separation of temporal evolution from spatial variability. The resulting dataset provides meter-scale maps of air and surface temperature, vertical profiles of thermodynamic and wind structure, and land–atmosphere exchange measurements. Technical validation demonstrates strong agreement between independent measurements and quantifies reconstruction accuracy under varying sampling conditions. This dataset supports process-level studies of urban microclimate, evaluation of high-resolution micrometeorological models, and the development of spatiotemporal reconstruction and data assimilation approaches.

item.title: Digitalization of the genotypic and phenotypic information retained within the FEM grapevine germplasm bank
item.description:
Silvia Vezzulli, Paola Bettinelli, Daniela Nicolini, Daniele Migliaro, Giulia Betta, Geovani Luciano de Oliveira, Carlotta Pirrello, Silvano Clementi, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08482-8
Abstract The Fondazione Edmund Mach (FEM) maintains a grapevine germplasm bank consisting of 3,065 grapevine accessions that supports long-term conservation and utilisation of crop genetic diversity. In addition to acquisitions, the germplasm includes advanced crossbreeding selections developed to improve grape quality and introgress tolerance and resistance traits. This objective highlights the importance of verifying accession identity through standardized molecular profiles, complemented by ampelographic characterization when necessary. A systematic inventory of the germplasm was undertaken and a comprehensive ontologization of all accession-related data and metadata was carried out in the context of FAIR (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability) compliance. This overarching survey led to the published FEMVitisDataset encompassing 2,905 accessions, resulting in the identification of 1,931 unique profiles. Of these, 915 were classified as novel, as no exact or near-exact genetic match was found across the consulted reference databases. By providing accession-level passport data, validated SSR profiles, and associated phenotypic information, the FEMVitisDataset expands the documentation of grapevine diversity and represents a valuable resource for germplasm management, genetic studies, and modern breeding programs integrating molecular and phenotypic information.
